applicationPortal.value: Step 1: apply through CIM's online application portal. Step 2: upload the required prescreening video for Piano by the December 1 deadline. Step 3: upload all required application materials, including performance resume, 250-500 word essay, one-minute video introduction recorded inside the application system, transcripts, and recommendation information. Step 4: complete the online theory examination after prescreening decisions are released in late December; Master of Music applicants are among the applicants required to take the online theory exam. Graduate transcript note: Master of Music applicants submit the bachelor's degree transcript. Recommendation note: all conservatory applications require two confidential recommendation letters from qualified people unrelated to the applicant; recommendation letters are due January 15.

applicationFee.value: Application fee: $125 nonrefundable, submitted online with the application. Late fee timing: the application fee increases to $175 at 12:00am on December 2. Fee waiver note: CIM's published application-fee waiver language on the audited page is for eligible first-time freshman and undergraduate transfer applicants; the page does not publish a graduate application fee waiver route.

auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: Piano requires a prescreening video. CIM strongly urges applicants to submit applications well before the December 1 deadline. Recording specifications: each piece of repertoire must be unedited and recorded separately; media files should be no larger than 5GB; use a single fixed-focus camera with no zooming that displays a full-body view of the performer and instrument; recordings must be uploaded into CIM's online application system, and CIM asks applicants not to mail CDs or DVDs. Video introduction: all applicants record a one-minute video inside the application with full name, area of study, degree sought, and a response about what a successful music career would look like. Admission exam: Master of Music applicants take the online theory examination after prescreening decisions are released in late December; the theory exam is due February 1. Live audition dates: CIM lists February 8, February 15, February 22, and March 1, 2026 as in-person audition dates. Area-specific schedule note: the Live Auditions page says specific Fall 2026 Piano audition dates will be announced soon.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Must be played from memory. Prescreening repertoire: A J.S. Bach work featuring a fugue, such as Well-Tempered Clavier Preludes and Fugues, Toccatas, Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue, etc. Prescreening repertoire: Two contrasting movements from a Classical Sonata by Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven or Schubert. Prescreening repertoire: One Chopin etude of virtuosity. Prescreening repertoire: A Romantic OR 20th century work of your choice. Final audition repertoire: Must be played from memory. Final audition repertoire: A J.S. Bach work featuring a fugue, such as Well-Tempered Clavier Preludes and Fugues, Toccatas, Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue, etc. Final audition repertoire: Complete classical sonata by Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven or Schubert. Final audition repertoire: One substantial romantic work from the 19th century. Final audition repertoire: One work from the 20th or 21st century. Final audition repertoire: One Chopin etude of virtuosity. Additional repertoire notes: CIM encourages applicants to expand beyond the traditional canon where requirements allow flexible repertoire choices and points applicants to its underrepresented-composer resource database.

deadlines.value: Application opens: September 1, 2025. Application and prescreening video deadline: December 1, 2025. Application fee increase: 12:00am on December 2. Recommendation letters and transcripts due: January 15. Online theory examination due: February 1. In-person audition dates: February 8, February 15, February 22, and March 1, 2026. Admission decisions and scholarship awards: late March 2026. Graduate decision deadline: April 15, 2026. Spring entry deadline: October 1. Prescreening decisions: late December, after faculty review prescreening videos.

englishScores.value: Minimum scores: Scores required to schedule an audition by December 1 for Master of Music: TOEFL iBT 61; TOEFL Essentials 6.5; IELTS 6; PTE Academic 44; Duolingo 100. Minimum scores: Scores required to be considered for unconditional acceptance by March 1 for Master of Music: TOEFL iBT 79; TOEFL Essentials 9; IELTS 6.5; PTE Academic 53. Timing: applicants from countries where English is not an official language must submit English language test scores in the application by December 1; no audition will be scheduled without the required English proficiency exam; Duolingo scores submitted for audition scheduling must be accompanied by an official TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE Academic score by March 1. Validity: exams taken more than two years before the application period are not accepted. Exemptions: TOEFL/IELTS waivers are not guaranteed, but applicants with three or more consecutive years in an English-speaking institution are eligible to apply; waiver review occurs case by case after a complete application is submitted, and applicants should submit the request and application before December 1. Notes: minimum scores must come from one single test; CIM does not accept TOEFL MyBest scores; CIM may require additional language training if scores do not reflect actual English proficiency or if English skills are assessed as insufficient; Bachelor and Master of Music applicants accepted with TOEFL iBT 61-78 or IELTS 6 must enroll in CIM's English Language Training Program.

applicationPortal.value: Step 1: apply through CIM's online application portal for Master of Music in Collaborative Piano. Step 2: because prescreening recording is optional for MM Collaborative Piano, upload a recording only if desired; optional recordings should consist of selections from the audition repertoire. Step 3: upload all required application materials, including performance resume, 250-500 word essay, one-minute video introduction recorded inside the application system, transcripts, and recommendation information. Step 4: complete the online theory examination after prescreening decisions are released in late December; Master of Music applicants are among the applicants required to take the online theory exam. Graduate transcript note: Master of Music applicants submit the bachelor's degree transcript. Recommendation note: all conservatory applications require two confidential recommendation letters from qualified people unrelated to the applicant; recommendation letters are due January 15.

Fee waiver note: CIM's published application-fee waiver language on the audited page is for eligible first-time freshman and undergraduate transfer applicants; the page does not publish a graduate application fee waiver route.

auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: Collaborative Piano is listed under optional recordings; a prescreening recording is not required for MM Collaborative Piano, except that all DMA and Artist Diploma applicants must submit prescreening videos. Optional recording: if the applicant uploads a video recording, it should consist of selections from the audition repertoire. In-person requirement: CIM's Audition page says all applicants in Collaborative Piano require an in-person audition in Cleveland. Live audition dates: CIM lists February 8, February 15, February 22, and March 1, 2026 as in-person audition dates; the Live Auditions page says specific Fall 2026 Collaborative Piano audition dates will be announced soon. Audition logistics: a singer will be provided for live auditions in Cleveland; one of the three art songs should be prepared both to be played and sung, and CIM states this is not a vocal-talent test but a check of coaching-related multitasking, diction, and textual expression. Admission exam: Master of Music applicants take the online theory examination after prescreening decisions are released in late December; the theory exam is due February 1. Video introduction: all applicants record a one-minute video inside the application with full name, area of study, degree sought, and a response about what a successful music career would look like.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: No prescreening recording is required for MM Collaborative Piano; if a recording is uploaded, it should consist of selections from the audition repertoire. Final audition repertoire: Perform one solo piece of your choosing. Final audition repertoire: Choose one sonata from the following: Beethoven Sonata #5, Violin and Piano, Opus 24; Beethoven Sonata #7, Violin and Piano, Opus 30, #2; Beethoven Sonata #3, Cello and Piano, Opus 69; Brahms Sonata for Violin and Piano #2, Opus 100 in A major; Brahms Sonata for Violin and Piano #3, Opus 108 in D minor; Brahms Sonata for Cello and Piano #1, Opus 38 in E minor; Brahms Sonata for Cello and Piano #2, Opus 99 in F major; Debussy Sonata for Violin and Piano; Debussy Sonata for Cello and Piano; Franck Sonata in A major; Faure Sonata in A major, Opus 13. Final audition repertoire: Choose one concerto reduction from the following: Tchaikovsky Violin Concerto, Opus 35 in D major; Sibelius Violin Concerto in D minor, Opus 47; Mozart Violin Concerto #5, K. 219 in A major; Elgar Cello Concerto, Opus 85; Dvorak Cello Concerto, Opus 104 in B minor. Final audition repertoire: Choose one from the following three pieces: Kreisler, Songs My Mother Taught Me; Tambourin Chinois, Opus 3; Marche miniature Viennoise. Final audition repertoire: Choose three contrasting art songs to be played in the high/soprano key; German options include Brahms, Botschaft; Schubert, An die Musik or Du bist die Ruh; Schumann, Postlude of Frauenlieben und Leben or Dichterliebe; Strauss, Standchen; Wolf, Er ist's or Ich hab' in Penna. Final audition repertoire: French art-song options include Chausson, Le colibri or Les papillons; Debussy, Ariettes oubliees: C'est l'extase or Il pleure dans mon coeur; Duparc, Chanson triste; Faure, En sourdine; Poulenc, Fiancailles pour rire: Violon or Il vole. Final audition repertoire: English art-song options include Barber, Hermit Songs: St. Ita's Vision, The Monk and His Cat, or The Desire for Hermitage; Bridge, Love Went A-Riding; Copland, Twelve Poems of Emily Dickinson: Nature, the gentlest mother, Heart, we will forget him, or Going to Heaven! Final audition repertoire: Choose one aria from Mozart, Countess's Recitative/Aria, E Susanna...Dove Sono from The Marriage of Figaro, or Puccini, Musetta's Waltz, Quando m'en vo from La Boheme. Additional repertoire notes: A singer will be provided for live auditions in Cleveland; one of the three art-song selections should be prepared both to be played and sung.
